message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates, 35 mph on rural highways, 25 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• Construction zones: 15 mph unless otherwise posted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers 21+.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Yield” signs give right‑of‑way to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights only allowed on foggy days. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing regulations: minimum towing speed 25 mph, must have a tow bar or chain. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid handicap placard. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• In Texas, stopping is required in both directions. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used in many counties; fines are issued automatically. | TxDOT website | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Department of Insurance | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Regular updates on road conditions, construction, and new regulations. 3. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Driver’s license info, DUI laws, and enforcement notices. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances (e.g., parking restrictions, speed limits in city limits). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – no texting, no handheld calls. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re strictly enforced, especially in construction zones. - **Be mindful of school zones** – speeds drop significantly. - **Check your vehicle’s registration** – expired stickers can lead to fines. - **Use headlights** – even on clear days, it improves visibility. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
